Arkansas paid $1.23 billion in monthly Social Security benefits in December 2024
In December 2024, Arkansas paid $1.23 billion in Social Security benefits, with retired workers making up the largest portion by benefit dollars.
Arkansas paid $1.23 billion in Social Security benefits to beneficiaries living in the state in December 2024. This was an increase of $57.8 million, or 4.9%, from December 2023.
The Old-Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance program, commonly known as Social Security, provides monthly benefits to qualified retired and disabled workers, their dependents and survivors of insured workers. Eligibility and benefit amounts are based on a worker's Social Security-covered earnings and contributions rather than financial need. OASDI is separate from Supplemental Security Income, or SSI, which provides benefits based largely on limited income and resources and is funded through general federal tax revenues rather than employment taxes.
The approximate average monthly benefit paid to the 726,942 Social Security beneficiaries in Arkansas in December 2024 was about $1,693.
The benefit split for December 2024 was $928 million to retired workers (75.4%), $68.2 million to widow(er)s and parents (5.5%), and $234 million to disabled workers, spouses and children combined (19%).
Arkansas ranked 31st of 51 jurisdictions for total Social Security benefit dollars paid in December 2024 among the 50 states and the District of Columbia. Benefits paid equaled $404 per resident, which was $34 above the figure constructed across the 50 states and the District of Columbia for 2024.
Over the past ten years, Arkansas's December monthly Social Security benefit total increased by 61.7%, from $761 million in 2014 to $1.23 billion in 2024. The 2024 total exceeded the preceding ten-year average of $917 million by 34.3%. The lowest reported total was $761 million in 2014, and the highest was $1.23 billion in 2024; neither figure was tied. All series figures are nominal and not adjusted for inflation.
Among the five beneficiary categories, retired workers were the largest group by count in December 2024, followed by disabled workers.
SSA also reported that 531,244 beneficiaries in Arkansas were aged 65 or older in December 2024, representing 73.1% of all beneficiaries in the state.
The figures reflect Social Security beneficiaries in current-payment status as of December, with each beneficiary assigned to a state from SSA address records, which may use a representative payee’s address instead of the beneficiary’s home. Dollar amounts are published as December monthly totals, rounded to the nearest thousand, in nominal dollars not adjusted for inflation. Annual changes in the trend series represent year-over-year differences from the previous December.
